chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad narrated to us, from Ubaydillah ibn Musa al-Alawi, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Ibn Bakayr, from Zurara, from Abdul Malik ibn A'yun, who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far saying: 'For the Qa'im (the Rising One) is a concealment before he rises.' I asked: 'Why?' He said: 'He fears' and he pointed with his hand to his abdomen. He meant killing.

key_terms.الْقَائِم: The Rising One, a title for the Mahdi

ai.seo_question: Why does the Mahdi undergo concealment before his rise according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Nu'mani's *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Baqir clarifies that the Mahdi's pre-emergence concealment is a strategic precaution against assassination, specifically pointing to his abdomen as the vulnerable site. This establishes the theological basis for the 'Minor Ghaybah' as a period of protective hiding rather than mere absence, ensuring the Imam's survival until the divinely appointed time of uprising.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (19) Ali bin Ahmad narrated from Obaydillah bin Musa al-Alawi from Ahmad bin al-Hasan from his father from ibn Abu Bukayr from Zurara that Abdul Melik bin A’yun had said:
I heard Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (as) saying: “Al-Qa’im (as) disappears before his rising.” I asked: “Why?” He said: “He fears” and he pointed with his hand at his abdomen. He meant “killing”.
